ratings.reviewer_notes: Directly identifies PON1 and its Q192R polymorphism as associated with clopidogrel active-metabolite formation, platelet inhibition, and stent thrombosis.
Direct association study finding PON1 Q192R and CYP2C19*2 associated with high platelet reactivity and ischemic events during clopidogrel treatment.
Review-level pharmacogenetic context identifying CYP2C19 loss-of-function variants as major determinants of clopidogrel pharmacokinetics and platelet response.
Examines residual clopidogrel variability after controlling or excluding known polymorphisms, including CYP2C19, CYP3A5, ABCB1, and PON1, rather than discovering a direct new gene association.
Directly tests CYP2C19, PON1, and ABCB1 variants; CYP2C19*2 and loss-of-function carrier status predicted high platelet reactivity, while PON1 and ABCB1 did not.
Directly associates CYP2C19*2 with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and ABCB1 with failure of clopidogrel loading-dose adjustment; PON1 was not associated.
Direct pharmacogenomic association study implicating CYP2C19, PON1, ABCB1/MDR1, PEAR1, and rs12777823 in residual platelet reactivity or clopidogrel resistance.
Directly finds a CYP2C19 allele-dose association with platelet reactivity, high on-treatment reactivity, and outcomes; ABCB1 and PON1 were not significant.
Title directly concerns PON1 and clopidogrel efficacy, but no abstract is available to determine whether original association evidence was presented.
Directly associates CYP2C19 loss-of-function and PON1 Q192R variants with platelet inhibition and high platelet responsiveness during clopidogrel therapy.
Large prospective registry directly linking CYP2C19 variants with high on-treatment platelet reactivity and adverse outcomes after PCI; several other candidate genes were also evaluated.
Directly finds CYP2C19*2 and *3 associated with clopidogrel response variability, while CYP2B6, CYP3A4, CYP3A5, ABCB1, PON1, and P2Y12 variants were not predictive.
Clinical pharmacogenetics guideline directly addresses CYP2C19 genotype effects on clopidogrel activation, platelet inhibition, cardiovascular risk, and genotype-guided therapy.
Direct pharmacogenomic study associating CYP2C19*2 with clopidogrel nonresponse and CYP2C19*17 with enhanced antiplatelet activity; other tested genes were nonsignificant.
Primarily evaluates adjunctive cilostazol in clopidogrel-treated peripheral artery disease; CYP2C19, ABCB1, PON1, and P2RY12 were genotyped, but no genotype-response association is reported.
Directly identifies CYP2C19 metabolic genotype as an independent predictor of clopidogrel platelet reactivity; PON1, ABCB1, CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP3A4, and CYP3A5 were not associated.
Direct pediatric study in Kawasaki disease linking CYP2C19 loss-of-function alleles and PON1 192Q with high on-treatment platelet reactivity; ABCB1 was also tested.
Direct pharmacogenetic analysis associating ABCB1 3435 TT and CYP2C19 reduced-function alleles with reduced clopidogrel effect and increased cardiovascular events.
Directly evaluates combined CYP2C19, PON1, and ABCB1 mutations and reports associations with platelet aggregation and recurrent thrombosis during clopidogrel therapy.
Directly demonstrates that reduced-function CYP2C19 alleles are associated with lower active-metabolite exposure, diminished platelet inhibition, and adverse cardiovascular events.

Directly associates CYP2C19 loss-of-function alleles and ABCB1 3435 TT with cardiovascular outcomes in clopidogrel-treated myocardial infarction patients; CYP3A5, P2RY12, and ITGB3 were nonsignificant.
Directly finds a gene-dose effect of CYP2C19 loss-of-function alleles on clopidogrel pharmacodynamics and ischemic events; ABCB1 and PON1 were not significantly associated.
